articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Images, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring unified multimodal reasoning that processes code, images, audio, and video within a single inference pass rather than routing to specialized sub-models. Benchmarks show a 38% improvement on ARC-AGI-2 over GPT-5's initial release, with significantly reduced hallucination rates. The model is available via API with a new streaming architecture that reduces time-to-first-token by roughly 50%.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which solved 88% of International Mathematical Olympiad 2026 problems at a gold-medal level, a significant jump from last year's results. The system combines enhanced chain-of-thought reasoning with a novel self-verification loop that formally checks proof steps using Lean 4 integration. The breakthrough signals meaningful progress toward AI systems capable of genuine mathematical discovery.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in BMW and Amazon Warehouses
articles.summary: Tesla's Optimus Gen 3 humanoid robot has started pilot deployments in BMW's Spartanburg plant and two Amazon fulfillment centers, performing bin-picking, parts transfer, and quality-inspection tasks. The new hardware revision features 28 degrees of freedom in each hand and a custom Tesla-designed vision transformer running on-device. Early reports indicate the robots sustain roughly 85% of human worker throughput on targeted repetitive tasks.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Electric Demonstrates Autonomous Construction Site Navigation
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics released a video and technical paper showing its electric Atlas robot autonomously navigating an active construction site, climbing ladders, stepping over debris, and delivering tool payloads to specific floors. The system uses a foundation world model trained on thousands of hours of construction-site video combined with real-time LiDAR SLAM. The company announced commercial pilot partnerships with three major US construction firms starting Q1 2027.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Claude Alignment Reports' — Publicly Auditable Safety Evaluations for Every Major Model Release
articles.summary: Anthropic announced a new transparency initiative requiring the publication of detailed alignment and safety evaluation reports for each major Claude model release, including red-team results, capability elicitation benchmarks, and catastrophic-risk assessments. The reports follow a standardized schema designed in collaboration with NIST and the UK AI Safety Institute. Industry observers see this as a potential template for the regulatory compliance frameworks emerging in the EU and US.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node for AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed it has begun high-volume manufacturing on its A14 (1.4nm-class) gate-all-around transistor process, with AI accelerator chips from Nvidia and Broadcom among the first customers. The node delivers a 25% performance gain and 35% power reduction over N2, which is critical for next-generation data center GPUs facing power-density constraints. Analysts expect the first commercial products on A14 to ship in early 2027.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance to Expand Brain-Computer Interface Trial to 50 Patients
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to expand its N1 brain-computer interface implant trial from the initial cohort to 50 patients with quadriplegia, following positive 18-month safety and efficacy data from the first participants. Patients demonstrated sustained cursor control, text entry at up to 32 words per minute, and preliminary robotic arm manipulation. The expanded trial will also evaluate a second-generation implant with double the electrode count.

articles.title: Figure AI and Microsoft Partner on Foundation Model for General-Purpose Humanoid Robot Control
articles.summary: Figure AI announced a partnership with Microsoft Research to develop a large-scale foundation model specifically for humanoid robot control, trained on simulation and real-world teleoperation data spanning hundreds of manipulation and locomotion tasks. The model uses a diffusion-based action prediction architecture and reportedly enables zero-shot transfer to novel household tasks with a 70% success rate in lab evaluations. The collaboration aims to ship an integrated system to early enterprise customers by mid-2027.
